issues.description: Three independent fixes (state collapse, stack reset, yield-ordering) are squashed into one diff without a regression test
issues.detail: The PR bundles three separate bugs into one commit: collapsing working/walking states, fixing the s.stack[0:] no-op, and moving s.state[k]=sorted inside the yield branch. Each deserves its own patch with reasoning, and the PR title 'Fix state reuse' demands a Sort-twice regression test that is absent. Split the patch and add the test.

issues.description: Collapsing working/walking into one state removes a distinction push() still relies on without stating the new invariant
issues.detail: The prior three-state machine separated 'children being expanded' from 'cycle-detection during push.' Merging into 'walking' makes the name describe two temporal phases, and push()'s LastIndexFunc cycle-detection branch now depends on a subtler unstated invariant. Either keep the states with clearer names or write the invariant down in a literate-grade comment.

issues.description: Moving cleanup into defer and making sorted-marker conditional on yield changes reuse semantics without justification
issues.detail: Cleanup-on-defer entangles iterator lifetime with sorter validity: if Sort() is called but the returned iter.Seq is never invoked, prior state lingers. Additionally, s.state[k]=sorted now only runs when yield succeeds, changing early-termination semantics. Both are likely fine given defer-clears, but the coupled invariant needs to be stated, not implied.

issues.description: Stack reset fix (clear + [:0]) is correct but uncommented; previous s.stack[0:] was a real no-op bug
issues.detail: The old s.stack[0:] sliced to full length and never reset the stack, leaving stale Node references that blocked GC. The replacement clear(s.stack); s.stack = s.stack[:0] is exactly right, but the code does not say why clear precedes truncate. One line of comment ('clear before reslice so retained Node references can be GC'd') would make intent legible.

issues.description: Rewritten state-machine comment contains typos ('visisted', 'if its')
issues.detail: The comment is now the canonical explanation of the two-visit DFS state model, and it has 'visisted' (should be 'visited') and 'if its' (should be 'it's'). Since the state machine just lost a state, this comment carries more load-bearing weight than before. Clean it up.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR fixes real defects — s.stack[0:] was a no-op that retained Node references, and the sorted-marker placement was off — but the change is under-audited and under-explained. Three independent fixes are squashed into one diff with no regression test for the headline 'state reuse' bug. Collapsing working/walking into a single state is defensible but removes a distinction push()'s cycle-detection still depends on, and the new defer-based cleanup couples reset timing to iterator lifetime without stating the invariant. Verdict: needs work — split the patch, add a Sort-twice test, fix comment typos, and write the invariant down.
